VIEW FROM ROAD TOWARDS ST. LAWRENCE RIVER

ON 


ISLE PERROT 


28 MILES FROM MONTREAL 


BOYS — JUNE 26TH TO AUGUST 7TH 
GIRLS — AUGUST 7TH TO AUGUST 28TH 


INQUIRE AT YOUR 
NEAREST Y.M.C.A. 


> 


SAFE SWIMMING 


LOCATION AND DESCRIPTION 

Camp Perrot is situated on the south shore of Ile Perrot looking out 
over the St. Lawrence River with Beauharnois on the left and the Ottawa 
and St. Lawrence merging on the right. One of the sights, at the camp, is the 
ships travelling up and down the river, in front of the camp, and entering 
the St. Lawrence waterways Soulanges canal to the right of the camp. 
The camp property is some forty-five acres in extent and has some 600 feet 
of shore line. 
SWIMMING 

There is a sandy shore where the campers swim. This sand extends 
into the water for about one hundred feet and becomes a hard clay bottom. 
The slope is very gradual and the swimming location is safe for beginners. 
On the other hand, skilled swimmers have plenty of opportunity and space 
for advanced swimming from the raft. The camp possesses four boats. 
PLAYING SPACE 

A considerable portion of the camp property is level ground and lends 
itself to all types of team games such as softball, football, etc. Extensive 
bush land is within walking distance of the camp, where campers can enjoy 
nature hikes, camping out, and various woodcraft games. 
A REGISTERED NURSE IN ATTENDANCE 

A registered nurse is in residence throughout the camp period. A daily 
health clinic is held to insure the safety and health of campers. 
DRINKING WATER 

deep artesian well, tested and approved, provides an abundance of 

pure drinking water. 
HOUSING 


Campers sleep in tents erected over wooden floors built well off the 
ground. Each camper is supplied with a straw tick. 


OO 
$$ 


A FARM EXPERIENCE 

The camp operates a large garden to provide for the camp table. 
Boys and girls are given the opportunity to work in the garden. The close 
proximity of many farms makes it possible for the campers to become 
familiar with the elements of farming. 


WHO MAY GO 

Any boy or girl 10 to 16 years of age. In order to provide a holiday 
for as large a number as possible campers are restricted to a maximum 
of two weeks. 


CAMP STAFF 

The Camp is supervised by Mr. R. H. Hanagan, who is Director of 
boys and girls’ camping program of the Montreal Y.M.C.A. 

Mr. Gordon Mackey will be the Resident Director of the boys’ camp. 
He has had a number of years camp experience as a camper, counselloz: and 
Section director of Kamp Kanawana. Mr. Mackey, who has spent the past 
two and half years as a Flying Officer in the R.C.A.F. has seen service in 
Africa, India, China, and other parts of the world. 

Mr. John Parker will return to the camp as Camp Manager, in which 
capacity he served last summer. Mr. Parker has had many years experience 
in camping and boys’ work. He is a teacher at Westhill High School. 

Mrs. P. Parr, who for the past two years has so ably served the camp 
as Chef, will return in this capacity. 


GIRLS' CAMP M : 

The girls’ camp will be supervised by an experienced directoress, 
adult program assistants and a qualified group of young women, who 
will act as tent-counsellors. See A Die Sed

SUN BATHING ON THE BEACH 


EQUIPMENT 

Each camper must come supplied with three warm blankets, pillow, 
toilet articles, towels, bathing suit, soap, and clothes suitable for camp. 
A list equipment will be mailed when the application is received. 


WEEK-END CAMPERS 

Working boys and girls can make arrangements through the nearest 
YMCA to go to the camp from Saturday afternoon to Sunday evening at a 
cost of $1.40. Each individual must provide transportation. 


TRANSPORTATION ARRANGEMENTS ‘ 
Campers will be taken by bus from the Terminus on Dorchester St. 


at Drummond to the camp and return. The cost of the round trip is $1.00 
and is paid with the fees at the YMCA. Conducted parties will leave every 
Wednesday at 10 a.m. and will return to the terminus at around 12.30 p.m. 
Cost 

Camp rates are $7.00 a week plus the cost of transportation which is 
$1.00 return. Fees and transportation are payable at the “Y” Branch. 
Parents wishing to do so may drive their children to the camp. 
CAMP MANAGEMENT 

Camp Perrot is under the supervision of the Camp Board of Management, 
of which Mr. O. H. N. Owens is chairman. Mr. Ernest Hammond is chairman 
of the Camp Perrot Program Committee.
